nodes.label: docs/canon/DESIGN_HISTORY.md — how this system was actually designed and built, 2026-05-07 → 2026-08-03: one timeline in six eras, fused from git_record.md and desktop_docs_record.md plus the verbatim user canon, with the eighteen numbered contradictions adjudicated after Era 6 and a resolved-status line for each. Interpretation, produced 2026-08-03 and unreviewed by the user: it holds no status above any other document, every statement holds only as far as its citation, and the selection and ordering are agent judgement. Nothing here is new research — every statement already exists in a source record and arrives with that record's citation.

The three sources, and what each can settle. docs/canon/raw/git_record.md covers 2026-05-07 → 08-01 — 74 commits, 30 refs, 91 git show reproduce commands — and settles what existed when, what changed, what was deleted, and whether a later state contradicts an earlier one; never who wrote prose. docs/canon/raw/desktop_docs_record.md covers 2026-05-25 → 07-12 — 20 desktop-only agent-written handoff/state docs, 6,719 lines, ~150 recovered user quotes — and settles the decision conversations git cannot see, the fortnight git_record's own G-2 calls missing; second-hand, an agent's report of a conversation. docs/canon/USER_CANON.md holds 803 verbatim human turns 05-14 → 08-03 plus 80 recovered rulings, and settles what the user actually said, verbatim, with [CHAT] as first-hand keystrokes and [DOC] as a quote that passed through an agent's transcription. The corpus has grown since: 803 turns to 08-03 is what raw/user_turns_all.jsonl held at b0fcadc, the snapshot this file was read against, and at HEAD the corpus is 920 turns, 2026-05-14 → 2026-08-05T14:43:34Z, with USER_CANON.md at 1,589 lines rather than 1,577; nothing here was re-read against the added turns. Both raw records stay on disk untouched as evidence — this file reorders them, it does not replace them.

Citation rule and authorship labels. Every statement keeps the evidence its source record carried: a git claim carries its git show <ref>:<path> command exactly as git_record.md gives it; a docs claim carries the desktop doc's filename and heading; a user quote carries date plus the quote, and where USER_CANON.md holds it that is said so the two files stay linked. A claim without its citation is a defect — a bug in this file, not a licence to repeat it. Labels are kept from both records and never silently upgraded. From git_record.md: [USER] (first-person design voice, terse human commit register), [AGENT] (AI footer, or the mechanical "feat: update <dir> (N files)" tooling format), [UNKNOWN] (undecidable from git — most May/June prose). From desktop_docs_record.md: [USER-STATED] (verbatim quote or attributed ruling), [USER-STATED — paraphrase] (attributed ruling, agent's wording), [AGENT-ASSERTED] (proposal, synthesis, or agent-run measurement), [UNCLEAR]. The difference matters: C-16 rests on a paraphrase for six weeks before a first-hand quote appears.

Precedence when the two records disagree about who decided something: first-hand chat > git blob > agent-written doc. A [CHAT] turn in USER_CANON.md outranks everything. A git blob proves a thing existed but can never attribute prose. An agent-written state doc is the only attribution evidence for the two chat blackouts (05-16 → 05-26 and 05-29 → 06-26) and is used as such — labelled second-hand, never upgraded silently. Where the records genuinely disagree, both readings appear and the better-evidenced one is named; the unsettled ones are collected at the end.

The blackouts are not the only gap: the extractor filters the whole record, end to end. tools/canon_extract.py:118-121 rejects any user record carrying a toolUseResult key or a tool_result content block before considering its text, so a [CHAT] absence is never by itself proof he said nothing, at any date, inside or outside a blackout. Desktop half — 127 turns, all of May and June plus 59 July and 1 August — is enumerated in full by raw/EXTRACT_REPORT_desktop.md: 620 tool_result rejects yielding zero characters of human text (min 0, max 0), and 0 records across all 71 files carrying both a text and a tool_result block, "provably empty of human prose", so the eras this file covers most heavily are not weakened by the filter. Laptop half — 793 turns, 2026-07-06 onward — is reported by raw/EXTRACT_REPORT.md as 2,530 tool_result rejects, never enumerated, its exhaustive false-negative check scoped to the text-matching rule, so for July and August absence has not been shown to mean silence. A [CHAT] gap before 07-06 is a real gap in the conversation; a [CHAT] gap after it may be an artefact of extraction. Both blackout eras fall in the first case.

The era map, 2026-05-07 → 2026-08-03, one timeline fused from two independent forensic records plus the verbatim user canon. Era 1, 05-07 → 05-24: frames and facets — the system arrives fully designed and starts shedding parts. Era 2, 05-25 → 06-14: the v2 rebuild pivot — references not copies, and the weights stop being emitted. Era 3, 06-15 → 06-28: facet reconciliation and the v3 harness — the spec that was never built. Era 4, 06-28 → 07-12: the native artefact build, and its condemnation by its own author. Era 5, 07-13 → 07-28: the v1 retrieval engineering era — the forensic arm becomes the product. Era 6, 07-29 → 08-03: audit, corpus, tag-first — and the canon audit that produced these records. 06-28 is a hinge day and appears in two eras: the commits that close era 3 and the 123-turn build session that opens era 4 happen on the same date. Each era runs in date order and closes with a "what diverged" section.

Era 1 — frames and facets, 2026-05-07 → 2026-05-24. Evidence asymmetry stated up front: the desktop doc corpus begins 05-25 so it cannot witness this era at all, USER_CANON.md records its first surviving human turn on 05-14 and a chat blackout 05-16 → 05-26, so almost everything rests on git alone and prose authorship is correspondingly undecidable. What was decided: the system arrives fully designed on 05-07 (a 52-file Neo4j indexing pipeline, a 12-entry decision log, a 280-line graph schema); the original graph spine; the controlled canonical vocabulary; the cluster-dimension rename of 05-11, the only [USER]-labelled item, giving the five words still in use — theme→topic, object_entity→entities, event_process→activity, time_relevance→temporal, information_need→evidence; the interpretation frames rule that the model must not see pipeline machinery (05-13); the five-facet tagging contract (05-14); the query interpretation layer's prompt/chunk symmetry (05-14); and the full-HERB pilot as the empirical basis (05-14). What was built includes the v1 retrieval scoring formula, preserved in a memory file on 05-15, [AGENT] quoting [USER]. What diverged: the canonical vocabulary was deleted with no mention on 05-13 (C-3); two extra scoring factors arrive between design and ship, 05-18 → 05-28 (C-12); the jockedev2 RAGAS series is written and then squashed away on 05-19 (C-11); and two undefended constants go into 255,288 edges (C-15).

Era 2 — the v2 rebuild pivot, 2026-05-25 → 2026-06-14. 05-25: the weight/retrieval redesign, then the live audit that shelved it — the audit measured against herb-eval is the empirical basis for everything after. 05-30: the v2 pivot, references not copies. 06-01: the three-tier semantic model, [UNKNOWN] but strongly user-shaped. 06-03 / 06-04: chunking and the cap — the chunk as a coherent episode, a materialized integer path, no overlap, and ≈3000 tokens as an explicitly labelled calibration seed. 06-09: weights are measured from geometry, never emitted by a model, and all facet weights ride ONE edge. 06-11: the re-cut — phrase nodes, no chunk description, and THE BUILD GATE, nothing coded until every part of the stage is decided. 06-12: the spine closes at Source → File → Chunk → Tag with everything else an attribute. 06-14: facets as relevance channels, and the thesis is done. What diverged: the shipped v1 scorer has seven factors and five hard gates (05-28); D10 is never retracted in place (C-1); the SQL-agent baseline is adopted and then silently un-adopted; and the five-facet set enters as an agent synthesis and is treated as canon.

Era 3 — facet reconciliation and the v3 harness, 2026-06-15 → 2026-06-28. 06-15 is the largest design landing in the repo (0efff16, "Separate repo into v1/ (frozen) and v2/ (active)", +750 design lines, and the first CLAUDE.md), carrying the closed graph spine decided 06-12, the coherent-episode chunking design, the mapping key as a declarative per-dataset settings file, and structural oracle quarantine. Also decided here: the v2 facet set and its per-facet extraction specs — the spec that was never built; the retrieval routing model; model contracts as a working draft with nine unsigned items (06-14); the three-arm eval harness (06-18 → 06-23) with arm independence and comment hygiene (06-23); the lucene baseline (06-21); three documents in one day on 06-25; and the chat record resuming on 06-27. What was built: the tagger, with facets abandoned (06-28), and the fourth facet set, the content profile (06-27). What diverged: the per-facet extraction spec was fully written and never built (C-7); DESIGN.md contradicts itself at the same commit (C-9); three tagger-model decisions with the third undocumented (C-10); the leaderboard-comparable anchor metric was specced, stubbed, then deleted (C-17); and design-bearing changes are hidden under tooling commit messages (C-18).

Era 4 — the native artefact build and its condemnation, 2026-06-28 → 2026-07-12. The 06-28 123-turn session is reconstructed turn-by-turn, and what pass 1 actually is has a code record; the pass-1 result is [AGENT-ASSERTED], gold-100, k=10, retrieval-only. 06-30 / 07-01 is pass 2 — dials, the exponential curve, and the relationships pivot. 07-06: the v1 arm is revived, renamed and restated. 07-12: the state of things, and the artefact_v1 audit. What diverged: C-7 is resolved here by the four-step bridge from the per-facet spec to a flat tag list; C-2's causal chain completes while the contradiction does not yet exist; the canon goes stale on 06-28 and the staleness is logged the same day (C-14); and a list of things specified in this era and never built closes it.

Era 5 — the v1 retrieval engineering era, 2026-07-13 → 2026-07-28, in which the forensic arm becomes the product. 07-15: the four-point rejection of the gate. 07-16: trust revoked, and the terminal becomes canon. 07-17 → 07-24: the usage catastrophes. 07-20 → 07-21: the vocabulary is reclaimed. 07-22: orchestrator mode and the adversarial panel. 07-23: normalization, the hybrid arm, and commit-means-push. 07-25 → 07-26: what the score is for, and which artefact is which. 07-28: the graph question again, and the full revert. What was built is the shipped artefact arm, [UNKNOWN]. What diverged: three canon rules and the arm that ships now disagree at HEAD, and there is a standing note on what git cannot supply for this era.

Era 6 — audit, corpus, tag-first, 2026-07-29 → 2026-08-03. 07-29: held-out generalization, on his terms. 07-30: what tags are for. 07-31: the fullest clustering specification, and a reversal. 08-01: tags-first ships, and is immediately rejected. 08-02: gold-blindness, and the canon audit. 08-03: the two machines' history is merged. What diverged: the full revert took the matched-budget work with it; cluster-K has never been on the load-bearing path; the arbitrary constants he predicted are unenumerated at the time of writing; and the graph question, asked seven times, is never answered.

The eighteen contradictions, adjudicated. C-numbers are fixed at discovery in git_record.md and are kept unchanged so existing references resolve; they are listed in numeric order, while git_record.md's own by-importance reading order was C-1 · C-2 · C-3 · C-4 · C-5 · C-6 · C-7 · C-8 · C-9 · C-10 · C-11 · C-12 · C-16 · C-17 · C-18 · C-13 · C-14 · C-15. Each entry gives the git evidence, the desktop-docs verdict, and one line of resolved status. Verdict vocabulary from desktop_docs_record.md §4: CONFIRMS / REFUTES / EXPLAINS / PARTLY EXPLAINS / NEITHER.

C-1 through C-5. C-1 — D10 reversed, content-in-graph → references-only: git shows dba1160's "D10 … (:Chunk).content stores the chunk text … Status. Active" against 296fc40's charge that the v1 chunker "consumed each record, rendered it to a prose string, stored the string as c.content, and that lossy derivative became the only surviving copy"; the docs EXPLAIN it — the un-retracted D10 is the user's frozen-v1-docs policy, "that shit is still true for THAT build". C-2 — the v2 design declared all v1 eval numbers invalid while the shipped arm is the v1 graph. C-3 — the controlled canonical vocabulary was deleted with no mention. C-4 — six of eight node labels and four of seven edge types disappeared. C-5 — "the chunk description is dead", except in the arm that ships.

C-6 through C-12. C-6 — the condemned v1 facets returned under new names. C-7 — the per-facet extraction spec was fully written and never built. C-8 — entity decomposition specified, then reversed. C-9 — DESIGN.md contradicts itself in two places at the same commit. C-10 — three tagger-model decisions, each superseding the last, the final one undocumented. C-11 — six commits of measured results were squashed away. C-12 — "seven factors": the claim is correct.

C-13 through C-18. C-13 — "the model emits no numbers, ever" against the arm that ships. C-14 — canon describes a build state that no longer exists. C-15 — two constants that no artifact in git ever derives. C-16 — "no hard filters anywhere in ranking", written against a v1 that was full of them. C-17 — the leaderboard-comparable anchor metric was specced, stubbed, then deleted. C-18 — design-bearing changes routinely hidden under tooling commit messages.

The resolved-status table and its tally. Genuine silent drop: 3 — C-3 (an entire subsystem removed with one table cell, no user statement in any source), C-11 (of the commit record, not the knowledge — the negative finding shaped the v3 metric choice), C-14 (of the fix: canon went stale 2026-06-28, staleness logged the same day, repair never applied). Documented reversal: 6 — C-1, C-6 (out 05-30, in 06-25 on the argued fact-vs-kind distinction, out again 06-27, reconciliation still open), C-7 (four user-driven steps from per-facet spec to flat list, ending at [t52] "lean graph, live facets"), C-8 (attribution upgraded from [UNKNOWN] to the user's own node/attribute rule), C-16, C-17 ("this is ONLY RAGAS", said twice — a user decision, not a silent drop, though the unweighed consequence stands). User decision misread as drift: 3 — C-2 (a declared forensic contrast arm, gated behind sign-offs that never came, that became the reported system), C-5 (the rule is the user's and governs v3; the surviving description path is v1's), C-13 (the numeric-facet arm is kept because it violates the rule). Not a contradiction, verified: 3 — C-12, C-15 (α and 0.50 underived, the 3000-token sweep a deliberate deferral never executed), C-18 (record-keeping, the mechanism explained by long uncommitted stretches). Split across two statuses: 3 — C-4, C-9, C-10. Total 18. Live at HEAD: C-2, C-5, C-9, C-10, C-13, C-14, C-15, C-16, C-17, C-18, where git_record.md's own live list was C-2, C-5, C-9, C-13, C-14 and the desktop verdicts plus the 08-01 HERB_TAG_FIRST regime extend it. "HEAD" there means 6730d13, 2026-08-03, and two of the ten have closed since: C-16 when bb95e4b deleted HERB_TAG_FIRST, and C-15's enumeration half when v3/CONSTANTS.md inventoried 305 constants — the values themselves stay underived, so C-15 is narrowed, not closed. The other eight were not re-checked against 8c8c787.

Where the two records disagree, and the seven that the precedence rule (first-hand chat > git blob > agent-written doc) resolves cleanly. 1 — the dates of the 07-01 quotes: chat wins, the conversation ran 06-27 → 07-01 and the doc dates the write-up rather than the turns, which affects the condemnation of pass 1, the relationships pivot, the exponential curve, "fuzzy means embedded", and the dials framing. 2 — who owns the v2 five-facet set: docs win, the 05-31 facet design labels it [AGENT-ASSERTED] and the 06-25 doc has the user disowning it, "the user never hard-approved the specific five, and it hollowed the tag"; load-bearing for C-6 and C-7. 3 — C-8's attribution: docs win, three verbatim 06-12 quotes make the node/attribute rule the user's own, and git cannot attribute prose at all. 4 — C-4's :NEXT claim: docs win, the 05-25 live audit shows :NEXT was never populated and all 33 files are dispatch_mode=parallel, so git's inference is partly refuted by measurement. 5 — C-1's residue: docs win, it is the user's explicit frozen-v1-docs policy. 6 — C-17's cause: docs win, "this is ONLY RAGAS" said twice and emphatically is a user decision, though the consequence git identified still stands untouched. 7 — C-6's novelty: docs win, the 06-27 content-profile recovery was argued two days earlier, so git's "appears nowhere before it" is true of git alone and false of the full record.

The eight items where the two records genuinely conflict or both fall silent, and this document picks no winner. 1 — graph magnitudes: the 05-14 pilot reports 5,843 chunks selected, 255,288 :HAS_TAG edges and 25,896 unique tag names, while the 05-25 live audit against herb-eval reports :Chunk×4,869, :Tag×24,804, :HAS_TAG×230,321 — eleven days apart, every figure lower, and whether the graph was rebuilt, whether the pilot counted selection rather than the persisted end state, or whether one measurement is simply wrong cannot be told from either record; every downstream percentage is quoted against one base or the other without saying which. 2 — w_facet distinct values, 19 or 21: the desktop record contradicts itself, one doc saying 21 across 255k edges, the same day's audit 19 over 230k, and a third preserving the triple as 76 / 21 / 86; git carries only the 21. 3 — whether max-then-sum was "never repudiated": git traces it unbroken from retrieval.ts to artefact_v1.py, while USER_CANON §4 carries [CHAT] 07-23 "are you fucking shitting me!? it's NOT normalized AND it's \"summed\"? what fucking idiot combo is that!?" and, minutes later, "the difficult and relative part of them was how much they should matter/guide etc, not fucking if they are normalized and summed or not" — both his, and genuinely ambiguous. 4 — which framing governs facets, the 06-28 categorical or the 06-27/07-01 dials: both records agree it is open and neither closes it, and two parallel sessions ran unaware of each other, so an agent arbitrating its own precedence is not evidence. 5 — the interpreter model sequence does not reconcile: MODEL_CONTRACTS §0 "same LLM" (Mistral Large), interpreter.py's meta/llama-3.3-70b-instruct, artefact_v1.py's claude-haiku-4-5, plus 90d1074's "glm-5.2 interpreter" which C-10 does not include; no source states why the shipped arm's interpreter became Haiku, and the adjacent 07-18 chat is about the judge. 6 — whether the pass-1 gold-100 output folders were deleted and by which commit: the desktop record says 69115e0, git_record describes only what that commit adds, so it is unverified from git — which matters because every pass-1 number then survives only inside the desktop docs with no run directory behind it. 7 — how severe C-2 is: git calls it the largest live contradiction in the repo, the desktop record calls it drift after 07-12 rather than a decision inside the window, and [CHAT] 07-26 supports the milder reading while the canon lines at HEAD support the harsher one. 8 — shared silences neither record can fill: why qt.scopeWeight was introduced, why the built tagger is z-ai/glm-5.1, prose authorship generally (footers appear on only eight commits), how the corpus reached the machine (an unreachable stash of 1,550,956 insertions), and what the DATA_README shipped by 7879dfe says about cross-arm metric validity, read by neither pass and governing whether any Era 5 number may be quoted comparatively.

Provenance of this document. It is a reorganisation of two existing forensic records into one chronology: no git object was read for it, no document was re-verified, no measurement was taken, and no conclusion appears here that is not already in a source record. Where the two records disagree both readings are shown and the precedence rule decides, or in the eight unsettled cases nothing decides. Sources, all read in full: git_record.md (1,760 lines; 74 commits across 30 refs, 91 reproduce commands, items labelled [USER]/[AGENT]/[UNKNOWN], contradictions C-1…C-18, gaps G-1…G-10); desktop_docs_record.md (1,575 lines; 20 desktop-only design docs — 6 handoffs and 14 state docs, 6,719 lines of source — 2026-05-25 → 07-12, labelled [USER-STATED]/[USER-STATED — paraphrase]/[AGENT-ASSERTED]/[UNCLEAR], ~150 recovered quotes, and a verdict on each of C-1…C-18); and USER_CANON.md (1,577 lines, 803 verbatim human turns 05-14 → 08-03, read as cross-reference only — both figures the b0fcadc snapshot, correct for it, while at HEAD the file is 1,589 lines and the corpus 920 turns to 2026-08-05). Untouched: nothing under docs/canon/raw/ was modified and USER_CANON.md was not modified; both raw records remain on disk as evidence and remain the authority — where this file and a raw record differ, the raw record wins. Not opened: v3/data/questions.jsonl, gold100.jsonl, heldout100.jsonl and 10smoke.jsonl, per [CHAT] 08-02, so every question-set figure quoted here (1,514 = 815 + 699; the citation distribution min 11 / median 52 / mean 71 / p90 170 / p99 298 / max 683; the near-twin product names) is reproduced from inside a source record, not from the data.
